A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spotter, OU@ε, and Prototypical Relearning Attack research. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original unlearning and relearning experiments on CIFAR, Tiny-ImageNet, CASIA-WebFace, and transformer classifiers, together with ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds CLIP/ImageNet results, forget-adjacent retained-sample evaluation, and additional retraining results.

M1.justification: The core Spotter losses and PRA algorithm remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds a CLIP adaptation that freezes the text encoder and text embeddings, updates only the visual encoder, and applies masked distillation and dispersion through CLIP class probabilities and image embeddings.

E1.justification: v4 adds ImageNet classification using pretrained CLIP ViT-B/32, extending the existing image-classification coverage. CIFAR, Tiny-ImageNet, CASIA-WebFace, sequential unlearning, and severe class-forgetting scenarios were already evaluated in v3 and remain present.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Retrain with PRA to the face-recognition Grad-CAM comparison; v3 showed retraining only without attack there. The nine main unlearning baselines and the comparator sets in the matched quantitative experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate the closest 2%, 5%, and 10% of retained CIFAR-10 test samples using original-model feature proximity to the forget prototype, and unlearn ten randomly selected ImageNet classes with CLIP-specific PGD generation. Previously stated CIFAR settings, perturbation budgets, and PRA sampling and retention constraints remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A examines whether OU@ε reflects accuracy on forget-adjacent retained samples. Figure 4 extends the existing case study with retraining-under-PRA activation maps. The earlier coefficient, interpolation, perturbation, attack-sample, sequential-unlearning, and forget-ratio analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages for the main comparison and the highest attack accuracy across 500 trials per query-size scenario for SalUn plus Spotter. New Table 5 follows the existing three-run averaging practice; no new uncertainty estimation, significance testing, or changed repetition count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 fills previously blank retraining OU@ε entries with 0.2384 for CIFAR-10 and 0.2545 for CIFAR-100. New Table 3 reports CLIP Spotter forget-test accuracy 0.00%, retained-test accuracy 55.00%, and OU@ε 0.0141. Table 5 adds nearby-retained accuracies, including Spotter's 77.22%, 78.67%, and 80.56%. Figure 4 adds retraining-under-PRA outputs; matched earlier numerical results are otherwise retained.

T1.justification: The perturbed-set and OU@ε definitions, masked softmax, prototype-to-classifier derivations, and objective equations remain unchanged. The new motivation and discussion introduce no formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a retain-data-free over-unlearning metric, few-shot PRA, and plug-and-play Spotter combining masked distillation with dispersion. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 expands the distinction between behavioral class removal and retraining equivalence, and explicitly states the absence of formal guarantees and coverage of arbitrary subset, attribute-level, limited-access, or adaptive attacks. Appendix A interprets OU@ε as a local-distortion proxy. Section 5.2 also replaces the head-only explanation of Boundary Expand with a shadow-class and residual-feature explanation.

D1.justification: v3 supplies settings and hardware/software information but no code-access statement. v4's new Software and Data section announces source code for OU@ε, PRA, and Spotter, including training, unlearning, evaluation scripts, and instructions, substantially expanding documented access to reproduction resources. CLIP-specific implementation choices are also added; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for certified removal, UMAP, CLIP, defensive diffusion unlearning, and quantization-related unlearning failure, and develops behavioral-versus-certified unlearning positioning in Section 6. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata or consolidate the duplicated Wang reference rather than changing cited research.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the opening motivation, edits language throughout, introduces motivation subheadings and a Discussion section, and adds acknowledgements and Software and Data text. It reorders the existing ablation discussion and updates affiliations and the publication notice, while preserving most of the narrative and method exposition.

P2.justification: v4 adds the CLIP and nearby-retained tables and a Retrain-with-PRA column in Figure 4. Existing tables are compacted and renumbered, Figure 5 is relocated, and UMAP displays are resized. Most visual content and table structures remain recognizable and unchanged in substance.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful empirical support for the local-retention motivation, demonstrates a CLIP application, clarifies the objective and limitations, and improves code-access information. These are bounded gains: the CLIP experiment does not evaluate PRA robustness, and Appendix A's unqualified highest-local-accuracy claim needs correction because retraining outperforms Spotter on all three subsets in Table 5. The core method and earlier evidence remain stable.
